title: The Bhangi misl
hookLine: the strongest early misl, holding Lahore and Amritsar for a time

lines: A BAND THAT HELD A CITY.
cards: A huge bronze cannon sits on a street in Lahore. Tradition says people in the Punjab once had a nickname for it, a name that had nothing to do with whoever cast it.
They named it after the Sikh band that held it: the Bhangis' gun. A band that could keep hold of a gun like that, in a city like Lahore, was no small band. Today: the Bhangi misl.

teach.h: A NAME THAT CAME FROM A NICKNAME.
teach.b: Start with the name. Tradition says it came from one of the band's early leaders, who was fond of bhang, a drink made from hemp, and the nickname stuck to the whole misl.
Sikh histories tell it lightly, and the name outlived the habit: a nickname can outlast anyone remembering why. Second, reach.
In the way Sikh histories tell it, the Bhangis grew fast after the hard century, and their chiefs held land across a wide stretch of the Punjab.
In Amritsar, tradition says, they built a fort and held parts of the Guru's city.

teach.h: LAHORE AND AMRITSAR IN BHANGI HANDS.
teach.b: When the Dal Khalsa took Lahore, Bhangi chiefs were among those who shared and ruled it. The governor's city and the Guru's city, with one misl's riders in both. Third, the gun.

teach.h: THE GREAT GUN THAT CARRIED THEIR NAME.
teach.b: Tradition says the Bhangis captured the great cannon, and it stayed with them long enough to carry their name, a sign of their strength. Fourth, the part in today's line.
It didn't last. The later Bhangi chiefs were not the riders their fathers had been, as Sikh histories tell it, and they quarreled with each other.
In time Lahore passed to another misl's leader, a young man you'll meet later on this path. Amritsar too. Strength gathered in one generation was spent in the next.
The Bhangis were real, and they were strong. For a time.

how: Sikhs meet the Bhangi misl in Sikh histories and in stories about Lahore and Amritsar, where the band's fort and the great gun are remembered.

games.q: you're a Bhangi chief. your fathers won Lahore. your cousins want a bigger share. what happens next, in the way Sikh histories tell it?
o: the chiefs stand together and keep the city.
the chiefs quarrel, and the city passes to another misl.
the chiefs hand the city back to the old governor.
games.why: the later Bhangi chiefs quarreled, and in time Lahore passed to another misl's leader. strong, for a time.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you're strong in right now, a skill, your health, a friendship, and be glad of it for a few breaths.
Then gently notice its edges, what it depends on and what might change it, holding both the strength and the limit without fixing anything. If you pray, rest in Waheguru as you go.

wordCard.voice: bhang, the drink made from hemp that gave the misl its name. Its chiefs held parts of Lahore and Amritsar and the great gun, until the strength passed. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi for Bhangi, the misl's name, which tradition links to bhang.

carryVoice: Your line: strong, for a time. Even a great gun changes hands. See you tomorrow.
